category: Physics interfaces VII: chemical species, electrochemistry, plasma, semiconductor, particle tracing, optimization & mathematics
description: Remaining physics families: Chemical Reaction Engineering (Transport of Concentrated Species, Chemistry, Nernst-Planck, Reacting Flow, species boundary conditions), the electrochemistry modules (Primary/Tertiary Current Distribution, Lithium-Ion Battery, Fuel Cell, Corrosion, Electrodeposition and their electrode/electrolyte nodes), Plasma (Plasma, Drift Diffusion, ICP, Boltzmann two-term), Semiconductor features, Particle Tracing (Charged Particle Tracing, Mathematical Particle Tracing, releases, walls, forces), the Optimization Module interfaces and topology/shape features, and the Mathematics branch (Weak Form PDE, Wave Form PDE, ODE interfaces, Events, Curvilinear Coordinates, Wall Distance, Deformed Geometry, weak contributions and constraints, Equation View).

tools.name: Transport of Concentrated Species (tcs)
tools.description: Solves mass fractions of all species in a mixture where no species is a dilute solute - gas mixtures in reactors, combustion, fuel-cell channels, drying air - using Fick's law with mixture-averaged diffusivities, the Maxwell-Stefan equations, or a mixture-averaged formulation with thermal diffusion, and mixture density from the ideal gas law or user data. One species is eliminated by the mass constraint (sum of fractions = 1); couples to flow through Reacting Flow and to Chemistry for reaction rates and properties.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Chemical Species Transport > Transport of Concentrated Species (tcs); API: physics().create("tcs", "ConcentratedSpecies", "geom1")

parameters.name: Species names / From mass constraint
parameters.description: List of species; the one computed from the constraint.

parameters.name: Diffusion model
parameters.description: Mixture-averaged | Fick's law | Maxwell-Stefan (with binary diffusivity matrix).

parameters.name: Transport Properties node
parameters.description: Density (ideal gas / Chemistry), velocity field, diffusivities, molar masses.

parameters.name: Reaction / Reaction Sources
parameters.description: Domain reaction rates; Mass Fraction, Flux, Inflow, Outflow boundaries.

tools.notes: Requires the Chemical Reaction Engineering Module (also in Battery, Fuel Cell, Corrosion, Electrodeposition, Plasma and CFD modules). Use Transport of Diluted Species (already catalogued) when one solvent dominates.

tools.name: Chemistry (chem)
tools.description: Global/domain-level interface that holds a reaction mechanism (species and reactions with Arrhenius or user-defined rate constants, equilibrium reactions, electrode reactions) and computes species and mixture properties - reaction rates, heat of reaction, mixture density, viscosity, thermal conductivity, diffusivities - from thermodynamic data (built-in or the Thermodynamics node with property packages) for use by the transport, flow and heat interfaces. It is the space-dependent companion of Reaction Engineering and can be generated from it with 'Generate Space-Dependent Model'.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Chemical Species Transport > Chemistry (chem); API: physics().create("chem", "Chemistry", "geom1"); chem.create("rea1", "Reaction", -1)

parameters.name: Reaction nodes
parameters.description: Formula (e.g. A + B => C), rate constant (Arrhenius A, n, E) or user rate, reversible/equilibrium options.

parameters.name: Species nodes
parameters.description: Thermodynamic and transport properties per species (from Thermodynamics or user).

parameters.name: Mixture properties
parameters.description: Mixture type (ideal gas, liquid, concentrated), reference/mixture-averaged property models.

parameters.name: Calculate transport properties
parameters.description: Enable to expose chem.D_..., chem.mu, chem.k for coupling.

tools.notes: Requires the Chemical Reaction Engineering Module (or Battery/Fuel Cell/Corrosion/Electrodeposition/Plasma modules). Species concentrations are Model Inputs of chem: point them to the tds/tcs variables so rates use the local values.

tools.name: Nernst-Planck Equations (npe) / Nernst-Planck-Poisson Equations
tools.description: Ion transport interfaces: Nernst-Planck Equations (npe) solves diffusion, convection and migration of charged species with electroneutrality (potential from charge balance) for electrolytes, ion exchange membranes and electrokinetic flows; the Nernst-Planck-Poisson Equations multiphysics interface instead couples Transport of Diluted Species with Electrostatics (Poisson's equation) through the Potential Coupling and Space Charge Density Coupling nodes to resolve electric double layers, nanochannels and semiconductor-like charge separation.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Chemical Species Transport > Nernst-Planck Equations (npe); or Nernst-Planck-Poisson Equations (tds + es + couplings); API: physics().create("npe", "NernstPlanck", "geom1"); multiphysics().create("pc1", "PotentialCoupling", 3); multiphysics().create("scdc1", "SpaceChargeDensityCoupling", 3)

parameters.name: Species charges / mobilities
parameters.description: z_i and mobility (Nernst-Einstein from D_i by default).

parameters.name: Electroneutrality (npe)
parameters.description: Species eliminated by the charge-neutrality constraint.

parameters.name: Concentration / Current density / Potential boundaries
parameters.description: Electrode and inlet conditions.

tools.notes: Requires the Chemical Reaction Engineering Module or an electrochemistry module (npe also in the Microfluidics Module). Double layers are nanometres thick; mesh them with boundary layers.

tools.name: Reacting Flow (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined interfaces (Chemical Species Transport > Reacting Flow > Laminar Flow / Turbulent Flow; Reacting Flow in Porous Media; Reacting Flow, Diluted Species) that add a flow interface, a species transport interface (tcs or tds) and the Reacting Flow coupling node, which passes the velocity to the transport equations, the mixture density/viscosity back to the flow, and adds turbulent mixing (eddy diffusivity) and, for combustion, the eddy-dissipation reaction model. Used for reactors, mixers, combustors and catalytic converters.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Reacting Flow > Laminar Flow; API: physics().create("spf", "LaminarFlow", "geom1"); physics().create("tcs", "ConcentratedSpecies", "geom1"); multiphysics().create("rf1", "ReactingFlow", 3)

parameters.name: Coupling node settings
parameters.description: Turbulent Schmidt number, mass transfer to fluid density, turbulence-reaction interaction model.

parameters.name: Variants
parameters.description: Reacting Flow (tcs), Reacting Flow, Diluted Species (tds, coupling rfd1), Reacting Flow in Porous Media.

tools.notes: Requires the Chemical Reaction Engineering Module (turbulent variants also need the CFD Module). Stationary convergence often benefits from solving the flow first, then species (two study steps).

tools.name: Concentration / Flux / No Flux (species boundaries)
tools.description: The basic boundary conditions of Transport of Diluted Species (and Concentrated Species with mass fractions): Concentration prescribes c_i = c0 (Dirichlet, e.g. a reservoir or electrode at equilibrium), Flux prescribes the inward normal flux (a general flux, a mass transfer coefficient kc*(cb - c) for film resistance, or an electrode reaction current), and No Flux (default exterior) sets zero total flux (insulating wall). In 6.x Flux also offers 'Flux from reaction' via Chemistry.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Concentration (conc1) / Flux (flux1) / No Flux (nflx1 default); API: physics("tds").create("conc1", "Concentration", 2); create("flux1", "FluxBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: species / c0
parameters.description: Which species are constrained and their values.

parameters.name: Flux type
parameters.description: General inward flux J0 | External convection (kc, cb) | Reaction-based.

parameters.name: J0 / kc, cb
parameters.description: Flux value or mass transfer coefficient and bulk concentration.

tools.notes: Core product features. With convection, Inflow and Outflow are preferred at open boundaries; Concentration on an outlet causes spurious boundary layers.

tools.name: Reactions (domain) / Inflow / Outflow (species)
tools.description: Reactions is the domain node of the species-transport interfaces where volumetric production rates R_i (mol/(m^3 s)) are entered as expressions (mass-action kinetics, chem.R_i from a Chemistry node, Michaelis-Menten...); Inflow prescribes the concentration (or the total flux) of fluid entering through an inlet, and Outflow applies the convective-only condition n.(-D grad c) = 0 at outlets. Together with Transport Properties they form the minimal reactor model.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Reactions (reac1) / Inflow (in1) / Outflow (out1); API: physics("tds").create("reac1", "Reactions", 3); create("in1", "Inflow", 2); create("out1", "Outflow", 2)

parameters.name: R_c (per species)
parameters.description: Reaction rate expressions; 'Reaction rates from Chemistry' option.

parameters.name: Inflow type
parameters.description: Concentration | Flux (Danckwerts) with c0 values.

parameters.name: Mass transport to other phases
parameters.description: Reaction node option for interphase sources.

tools.notes: Core product features. Stiff kinetics benefit from the Chemistry interface's Jacobian contributions; Surface Reactions (sr) handles adsorbed species on boundaries.

tools.name: Porous Medium (species transport) / Partition Condition / Thin Diffusion Barrier
tools.description: Additional Transport of Diluted Species features: Porous Medium (with Fluid, Porous Matrix and optional Adsorption subnodes) applies effective diffusivity models (Millington-Quirk, Bruggeman, tortuosity), dispersion and retardation in porous domains; Partition Condition imposes a concentration jump c1 = K c2 at an interior boundary (immiscible phases, membrane partitioning); Thin Diffusion Barrier represents a thin membrane of given thickness and diffusivity as a resistive interior boundary. These cover chromatography, drug delivery, soil transport and membrane separation.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Porous Medium (porous1) / Partition Condition (pc1) / Thin Diffusion Barrier (tdb1); API: physics("tds").create("porous1", "PorousMedium", 3); create("pc1", "PartitionCondition", 2); create("tdb1", "ThinDiffusionBarrier", 2)

parameters.name: Effective diffusivity model
parameters.description: MillingtonQuirk | Bruggeman | Tortuosity | NoCorrection (porous1 > Fluid).

parameters.name: Partition coefficient K
parameters.description: Ratio of concentrations across the interface (pc1).

parameters.name: ds / D_thin
parameters.description: Barrier thickness and diffusivity (tdb1).

tools.notes: Porous Medium needs the Chemical Reaction Engineering, Porous Media Flow, Subsurface Flow or a related module; the Transport of Diluted Species in Porous Media interface pre-selects it. Partition Condition requires a slit (Form Assembly or interior boundary with discontinuous DOFs) - COMSOL handles this automatically.

tools.name: Electrode Surface Coupling / Electrode-Electrolyte Interface Coupling
tools.description: Coupling features that link electrochemical current-distribution interfaces to species transport: the Electrode Surface Coupling (tds/tcs boundary node) converts the electrode reaction currents of an Electrode Surface node into species fluxes by Faraday's law, and the Electrode-Electrolyte Interface Coupling and Porous Electrode Coupling (domain) do the same for porous electrodes, so that concentration-dependent kinetics (Tertiary Current Distribution behaviour) can be built from Secondary Current Distribution plus TDS.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Electrode Surface Coupling (esc1) / Porous Electrode Coupling (pec1); API: physics("tds").create("esc1", "ElectrodeSurfaceCoupling", 2)

parameters.name: Reaction Coefficients subnode
parameters.description: Coupled electrode reaction (from the current-distribution interface), stoichiometric coefficients and number of electrons.

parameters.name: Electrode reaction current source
parameters.description: Selection of the Electrode Surface / Electrode Reaction node whose current is converted.

tools.notes: Requires an electrochemistry module (Battery Design, Fuel Cell & Electrolyzer, Corrosion, Electrodeposition, Electrochemistry). The Tertiary Current Distribution, Nernst-Planck interface has this coupling built in.

tools.name: Primary Current Distribution (cd)
tools.description: Electrochemistry interface that solves Ohm's law for the electrolyte potential and (optionally) the electrode potential while treating electrode reactions as infinitely fast (no activation overpotential), so the current distribution is governed by geometry and conductivity only - the classic model for electroplating throwing power, cathodic protection screening and cell design at high current. It shares the feature set of Secondary Current Distribution (already catalogued), whose Electrode Reaction nodes add Butler-Volmer or Tafel kinetics.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Electrochemistry > Primary Current Distribution (cd); API: physics().create("cd", "PrimaryCurrentDistribution", "geom1")

parameters.name: Electrolyte / Electrode domain nodes
parameters.description: Ionic and electronic conductivities.

parameters.name: Electrode Surface with Electrode Reaction
parameters.description: Equilibrium potential only (primary) - the boundary potential is fixed by Eeq.

parameters.name: Electrolyte Current / Electrolyte Potential / Electric Ground / Electrode Potential
parameters.description: Cell-level boundary conditions.

tools.notes: Requires the Electrochemistry, Battery Design, Corrosion, Electrodeposition or Fuel Cell & Electrolyzer Module. The interface can be switched between Primary and Secondary in its settings (Current Distribution Type).

tools.name: Tertiary Current Distribution, Nernst-Planck (tcd)
tools.description: Most complete electrochemical interface: it solves the Nernst-Planck equations for every ionic species (diffusion, migration, convection) together with the electrolyte and electrode potentials and concentration-dependent electrode kinetics, with electroneutrality, supporting-electrolyte or water-based (with H+/OH- equilibrium) charge-balance options. Needed when concentration gradients and depletion govern the current (electrolysers, electrodialysis, plating from dilute baths, batteries with concentrated electrolyte).
tools.usage: Add Physics > Electrochemistry > Tertiary Current Distribution, Nernst-Planck (tcd); API: physics().create("tcd", "TertiaryCurrentDistributionNernstPlanck", "geom1")

parameters.name: Charge conservation model
parameters.description: Electroneutrality | Supporting electrolyte | Water-based with electroneutrality | Poisson (6.x).

parameters.name: Species
parameters.description: Names, charges, diffusivities (in the Electrolyte node), and the species eliminated by electroneutrality.

parameters.name: Electrode Surface > Electrode Reaction
parameters.description: Kinetics with concentration dependence (Butler-Volmer, concentration-dependent exchange current density) and stoichiometry.

parameters.name: Concentration / Flux / Inflow / Outflow
parameters.description: Species boundary conditions.

tools.notes: Requires an electrochemistry module. Nonlinear and often stiff; initialise with a Current Distribution Initialization study step (added by the Model Wizard) before the stationary/time-dependent step.

tools.name: Lithium-Ion Battery (liion)
tools.description: Battery Design Module interface implementing the Newman (Doyle-Fuller-Newman) pseudo-2D model: porous positive and negative electrodes with intercalating particles (solid diffusion in a 1D radial extra dimension), separator, binary electrolyte with concentrated-solution theory, Butler-Volmer intercalation kinetics, SEI growth and aging options, and thermal coupling; used for cell design, charge/discharge curves, impedance (AC Impedance studies), fast-charging and aging. Related interfaces: Battery with Binary Electrolyte, Lead-Acid Battery, Lumped Battery (lb, including its Two Electrodes single-particle option), Battery Equivalent Circuit, Battery Pack (bp); single-particle models also via the Thin Porous Electrode node (COMSOL 6.4 has no separate Single Particle Battery interface).
tools.usage: Add Physics > Electrochemistry > Batteries > Lithium-Ion Battery (liion); API: physics().create("liion", "LithiumIonBatteryMPH", "geom1")

parameters.name: Porous Electrode nodes
parameters.description: Electrode/electrolyte volume fractions, particle radius, material from the Battery material library (LiCoO2, LFP, NMC, graphite...), Porous Electrode Reaction with intercalation kinetics.

parameters.name: Separator / Electrolyte
parameters.description: Binary electrolyte properties (conductivity, diffusivity, transport number, activity dependence).

parameters.name: Electric Ground / Electrode Current / Electrode Potential
parameters.description: Applied current (C-rate) or voltage at the current collectors.

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Time Dependent with Initialization; AC Impedance for EIS; Stationary for equilibrium.

tools.notes: Requires the Battery Design Module. 1D models are standard for cell curves; 2D/3D add current collectors and thermal effects with Electrochemical Heating coupling to Heat Transfer.

tools.name: Hydrogen Fuel Cell (fc) / Water Electrolyzer (we)
tools.description: Fuel Cell & Electrolyzer Module interfaces for PEM, alkaline and solid-oxide cells: they combine current distribution in electrodes and membrane/electrolyte (proton or hydroxide conduction with water content dependence), gas-phase species transport (Maxwell-Stefan) in gas diffusion and catalyst layers, electrode kinetics (HOR, ORR, OER), water management and, with flow and heat interfaces, full stack models. Membrane, Gas Diffusion Electrode, Gas Diffusion Layer, Flow channel and Porous Electrode nodes describe the layers.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Electrochemistry > Fuel Cells and Electrolyzers > Hydrogen Fuel Cell (fc) / Water Electrolyzer (we); API: physics().create("fc", "HydrogenFuelCell", "geom1")

parameters.name: Cell type / electrolyte
parameters.description: Proton exchange, hydroxide exchange, oxygen ion (SOFC) in the interface settings.

parameters.name: Membrane / Gas Diffusion Electrode / Gas Diffusion Layer / Flow Channel nodes
parameters.description: Layer definitions with conductivities, porosity, permeability and gas mixture (H2, O2, H2O, N2).

parameters.name: Electrode reactions
parameters.description: Hydrogen oxidation/oxygen reduction with exchange current densities and reference concentrations.

parameters.name: Cell voltage / current
parameters.description: Electric Ground and Electrode Potential/Current on the current collectors; polarization curve via a parametric sweep.

tools.notes: Requires the Fuel Cell & Electrolyzer Module (5.6+). Two-phase water transport uses the Phase Transport interface coupling; heat generation couples through Electrochemical Heating.

tools.name: Corrosion / Electrodeposition (deforming electrode interfaces)
tools.description: Corrosion Module and Electrodeposition Module interfaces (Corrosion, Primary/Secondary/Tertiary; Electrodeposition, Primary/Secondary/Tertiary) that add to the current-distribution interfaces a Deforming Electrode Surface boundary feature coupled to Deformed Geometry, so the electrode moves with the metal dissolution or deposition rate computed by Faraday's law from the local current density; also Thin Electrode Surface features, galvanic couples, cathodic protection sacrificial anodes, and the Electrode Reaction kinetics expressed as polarization data. Used for galvanic corrosion, pitting/crevice, ICCP systems, plating uniformity and additive effects.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Electrochemistry > Corrosion, Deformed Geometry > Corrosion, Secondary (cdsec) or Electrodeposition, Deformed Geometry > Electrodeposition, Secondary (edsec); API: physics().create("cdsec", "CorrosionSecondary", "geom1") (type names follow the wizard entry)

parameters.name: Deforming Electrode Surface
parameters.description: Boundary node with dissolving/depositing species, molar mass, density, and the Electrode Reaction subnodes.

parameters.name: Nondeforming boundary / Symmetry for Deformed Geometry
parameters.description: Mesh constraints on the other boundaries.

parameters.name: Time Dependent with Initialization study
parameters.description: Initialises potentials before moving the geometry; Time Dependent, Fixed Geometry for quick checks.

parameters.name: Corrosion potential / polarization curves
parameters.description: Electrode kinetics from experimental Tafel data via interpolation functions.

tools.notes: Requires the Corrosion Module or Electrodeposition Module. Large shape changes need Automatic Remeshing in the time-dependent solver; the deposition rate variable (e.g. cdsec.des1.vdep) can be used for plating-thickness postprocessing. The API type string in this entry could not be confirmed in the COMSOL 6.4 registry; confirm it with Model Builder > File > Save As > Model File for Java.

tools.name: Electrolyte / Electrode / Porous Electrode (domain nodes)
tools.description: Domain material nodes of the current-distribution and battery interfaces: Electrolyte carries the ionic conductivity (and species transport properties in tertiary interfaces), Electrode the electronic conductivity of a solid conductor (current collector, bulk metal), and Porous Electrode combines both with volume fractions, effective-medium corrections (Bruggeman) and one or more Porous Electrode Reaction subnodes with specific surface area for reactions distributed through the volume (battery electrodes, gas diffusion electrodes, porous catalysts). Separator is the porous, non-reacting variant.
tools.usage: Physics > Secondary Current Distribution > Electrolyte (ice1 default) / Electrode (ece1) / Porous Electrode (pce1); API: physics("cd").create("pce1", "PorousElectrode", 3); pce1.create("per1", "PorousElectrodeReaction", 3)

parameters.name: sigmal / sigma
parameters.description: Electrolyte and electrode conductivities (from material or user).

parameters.name: epsl / epss
parameters.description: Electrolyte and electrode volume fractions of a porous electrode; effective conductivity correction model.

parameters.name: Porous Electrode Reaction
parameters.description: Kinetics (Butler-Volmer, Tafel, linear, user), equilibrium potential, exchange current density i0, active specific surface area av.

parameters.name: Double layer capacitance
parameters.description: Optional Porous Electrode/Electrode Surface capacitance for transient and impedance studies.

tools.notes: Requires an electrochemistry module. Electrode Surface (boundary) with Electrode Reaction is the surface analogue for planar electrodes.

tools.name: Electrode Surface / Electrode Reaction (Butler-Volmer)
tools.description: Electrode Surface is the boundary node of the current-distribution interfaces representing an electrode-electrolyte interface with a given electrode potential (phis,ext from a boundary condition, a total current, an average current density, or a circuit/external short); its Electrode Reaction subnodes define the charge-transfer kinetics - Butler-Volmer (i0, anodic/cathodic transfer coefficients or Tafel slopes), Tafel, linearized, concentration-dependent, limiting current, or user-defined polarization data - and equilibrium potential Eeq. The local current density iloc and overpotential eta are the key outputs.
tools.usage: Physics > Secondary Current Distribution > Electrode Surface (es1) > Electrode Reaction (er1); API: physics("cd").create("es1", "ElectrodeSurface", 2); es1.feature("er1").set("Eeq", ...)

parameters.name: Boundary condition (Electrode Surface)
parameters.description: Electrode potential phis,ext | Total current | Average current density | Electrode phase potential from another interface | Counter electrode.

parameters.name: Kinetics expression type
parameters.description: ButlerVolmer | AnodicTafel | CathodicTafel | Linearized | ConcentrationDependent | LimitingCurrent | UserDefined.

parameters.name: i0, alphaa/alphac (or Aa/Ac Tafel slopes), Eeq
parameters.description: Exchange current density, transfer coefficients, equilibrium potential (temperature-dependent options).

parameters.name: Stoichiometry / number of electrons
parameters.description: For coupling to species transport (Faraday's law).

tools.notes: Requires an electrochemistry module. Multiple Electrode Reaction subnodes on one surface model competing reactions (hydrogen evolution beside metal deposition). Variables: cd.es1.er1.iloc, cd.es1.er1.eta, cd.phis, cd.phil.

tools.name: Electric Ground / Electrode Current / Electrode Potential / Electrolyte Potential
tools.description: Cell-level boundary conditions of the electrochemistry interfaces applied on electrode (solid) or electrolyte boundaries: Electric Ground (phis = 0) and Electrode Potential (phis = phis0) fix the electronic potential on current collectors, Electrode Current prescribes the total current entering through a collector boundary (galvanostatic operation, C-rate cycling), and Electrolyte Potential / Electrolyte Current fix the ionic potential or current on electrolyte boundaries (reference electrodes, current feeders). Electric Insulation and No Flux are the defaults elsewhere.
tools.usage: Physics > Lithium-Ion Battery / Secondary Current Distribution > Electric Ground (egnd1) / Electrode Current (ec1) / Electrode Potential (epot1) / Electrolyte Potential (elpot1); API: physics("liion").create("ec1", "ElectrodeCurrent", 0); set("Itotal", ...)

parameters.name: phis0 / philpot
parameters.description: Prescribed electrode or electrolyte potential.

parameters.name: Itotal / inl
parameters.description: Total current or average current density for Electrode Current/Electrolyte Current.

parameters.name: Boundary condition type
parameters.description: Total current | Average current density | Electrode potential with external resistance (6.x).

tools.notes: Requires an electrochemistry module. A cell must have one ground-type condition for the electronic potential; polarization curves are obtained by sweeping E_cell or Itotal in an auxiliary sweep.

tools.name: Plasma (plas)
tools.description: Plasma Module fluid-model interface for non-equilibrium (low-temperature) discharges: it solves drift-diffusion equations for electron density and mean electron energy, transport of heavy species (mass fractions with multicomponent diffusion), Poisson's equation for the electric potential, and a full chemistry with electron impact reactions from cross-section data (imported LXCat files), surface reactions with secondary emission, and metastables. Typical applications: DC/RF capacitively coupled discharges, DBDs, glow discharges, microwave and inductively coupled plasmas (with the ICP multiphysics interface), plasma etching and deposition reactors.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Plasma > Plasma (plas); API: physics().create("plas", "ColdPlasma", "geom1")

parameters.name: Plasma Model node
parameters.description: Electron transport properties (from cross sections or Townsend coefficients), mean energy, gas pressure/temperature, reduced electric field options.

parameters.name: Electron Impact Reaction / Reaction / Surface Reaction / Species
parameters.description: Reaction mechanism with cross-section import and rate coefficients.

parameters.name: Wall / Ground / Metal Contact / Dielectric Contact / Terminal
parameters.description: Boundary conditions with secondary emission coefficients and surface charge accumulation.

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Time Dependent (RF cycles), Time Periodic (6.x, direct periodic steady state), Stationary for DC.

tools.notes: Requires the Plasma Module. Plasma problems are stiff: use the default BDF settings with tight tolerances and logarithmic formulation for densities. Drift Diffusion (dd), Heavy Species Transport (hs) and Electrostatics are the building blocks the Plasma interface bundles.

tools.name: Inductively Coupled Plasma (icp) / Microwave Plasma
tools.description: Plasma Module multiphysics interfaces that couple the Plasma fluid model with an electromagnetic interface: Inductively Coupled Plasma adds Magnetic Fields (frequency domain, coil-driven) and the Plasma Conductivity Coupling / Electron Heat Source couplings so that the RF coil deposits power ohmically in the electron gas; Microwave Plasma uses Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain instead for 2.45 GHz sources. Solved with the Frequency-Transient study (EM fields in the frequency domain, plasma in time).
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Plasma > Inductively Coupled Plasma (plas + mf + couplings) / Microwave Plasma (plas + emw); Study > Frequency-Transient; API: multiphysics().create("pcc1", "PlasmaConductivityMultiphysicsCoupling", 3); multiphysics().create("ehs1", "ElectronHeatSourceMultiphysicsCoupling", 3)

parameters.name: Coil (mf)
parameters.description: Excitation current/power of the ICP coil.

parameters.name: Plasma Conductivity Coupling
parameters.description: Passes the electron-density-dependent plasma conductivity to the EM interface.

parameters.name: Electron Heat Source
parameters.description: Passes the ohmic heating (and for microwaves the collisional absorption) to the electron energy equation.

parameters.name: Frequency-Transient study
parameters.description: Frequency for the EM part and time list for the plasma part.

tools.notes: Requires the Plasma Module (with AC/DC or RF Module features included). Power-controlled operation uses the coil's Power excitation with an integral constraint on the deposited power.

tools.name: Boltzmann Equation, Two-Term Approximation (be)
tools.description: Zero-dimensional Plasma Module interface that solves the electron Boltzmann equation in the two-term (Lorentz) approximation for a given gas mixture and reduced electric field (or mean energy), returning the electron energy distribution function, and from it the electron mobility, diffusivity and rate coefficients as functions of mean energy that the Plasma interface then uses instead of the Maxwellian assumption. Run with the EEDF Initialization, Reduced Electric Fields or Mean Energies study steps to tabulate the transport data.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Plasma > Boltzmann Equation, Two-Term Approximation (be); Study > Mean Energies / Reduced Electric Fields; API: physics().create("be", "BoltzmannEquation", "geom1")

parameters.name: Electron Impact Reaction nodes with cross sections
parameters.description: The same LXCat data as in the Plasma interface.

parameters.name: Reduced electric field / Mean electron energy sweep
parameters.description: Range of E/N (Td) or energies (eV) to tabulate.

parameters.name: Ionization degree / excited species fractions
parameters.description: Electron-electron collisions and superelastic collisions options.

tools.notes: Requires the Plasma Module. Export the resulting rate-coefficient tables or reference them from the Plasma interface's 'Electron transport properties: From Boltzmann equation' option.

tools.name: Semiconductor features (Analytic Doping Model, Metal Contact, Thin Insulator Gate, Trap-Assisted Recombination)
tools.description: The main nodes of the Semiconductor interface (already catalogued as semi): Analytic Doping Model / Geometric Doping Model define donor/acceptor profiles (constant, Gaussian, from a junction depth, or from a boundary with a decay length); Metal Contact applies ohmic or Schottky contacts (with thermionic emission and image-force barrier lowering) at a given voltage or terminal current; Thin Insulator Gate models a MOS gate as a boundary with oxide thickness and permittivity; and the recombination nodes (Trap-Assisted with Shockley-Read-Hall or explicit traps, Auger, Direct, Impact Ionization) set carrier generation-recombination. Together they build diodes, BJTs, MOSFETs, solar cells and photodiodes.
tools.usage: Physics > Semiconductor > Analytic Doping Model (adm1) / Metal Contact (mc1) / Thin Insulator Gate (tig1) / Trap-Assisted Recombination (tar1); API: physics("semi").create("adm1", "AnalyticDopingModel", 3); create("mc1", "MetalContact", 2); create("tig1", "ThinInsulatorGate", 2); create("tar1", "TrapAssistedRecombination", 3)

parameters.name: Doping: Impurity type, N_A0/N_D0, profile
parameters.description: Acceptor/donor concentration and distribution (Uniform, Gaussian with junction depth and peak).

parameters.name: Metal Contact: Type, V0
parameters.description: Ohmic | Ideal Schottky with work function and applied voltage or terminal current.

parameters.name: Thin Insulator Gate: d_ins, eps_ins, V0
parameters.description: Oxide thickness, permittivity and gate voltage.

parameters.name: Trap-Assisted Recombination: tau_n, tau_p / trap density
parameters.description: SRH lifetimes or discrete/continuous trap distributions.

tools.notes: Requires the Semiconductor Module. Use the Semiconductor Equilibrium study step to initialise before ramping voltages; the Semiconductor Optoelectronics, Beam Envelopes / Frequency Domain multiphysics interfaces add optical generation. Schrödinger Equation (schr) and Schrödinger-Poisson handle quantum-confined structures.

tools.name: Charged Particle Tracing (cpt)
tools.description: Particle Tracing Module interface that integrates Newtonian (or relativistic, or massless) equations of motion for ions and electrons in electric and magnetic fields from Electrostatics/Magnetic Fields solutions, with Electric Force, Magnetic Force, Collisions (elastic, ionization, charge exchange with a background gas), space-charge and beam-beam effects via the Particle Field Interaction couplings, and Monte Carlo releases. Used for ion optics, mass spectrometers, electron guns, beam physics, ion implantation and sputter deposition.
tools.usage: Add Physics > AC/DC > Particle Tracing > Charged Particle Tracing (cpt); Study > Time Dependent or Bidirectionally Coupled Particle Tracing; API: physics().create("cpt", "ChargedParticleTracing", "geom1")

parameters.name: Particle Properties
parameters.description: Mass and charge (from library species or user), formulation (Newtonian, Newtonian first order, relativistic, massless).

parameters.name: Electric Force / Magnetic Force
parameters.description: Fields from an existing interface (es.Ex...) or user expressions; time-dependent AC fields.

parameters.name: Release features
parameters.description: Release, Release from Grid, Inlet, Thermionic Emission, Release from Boundary, with velocity distributions (Maxwellian, cone, user).

parameters.name: Wall / Outlet / Symmetry
parameters.description: Freeze, Stick, Bounce, Disappear, Diffuse scattering, secondary emission.

parameters.name: Particle Field Interaction (multiphysics)
parameters.description: Electric Particle Field Interaction / Magnetic Particle Field Interaction couplings for space charge and beam self-fields.

tools.notes: Requires the Particle Tracing Module. Solve the fields first in a separate study, then the time-dependent particle study using that solution (Values of Dependent Variables > Not solved for). Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow (already catalogued) and Mathematical Particle Tracing share the release/wall features.

tools.name: Mathematical Particle Tracing (pt)
tools.description: General-purpose particle interface where the equations of motion are specified directly: Newtonian (user force), Lagrangian (user Lagrangian), Hamiltonian, or Massless (velocity field, i.e. streamline-like tracing), with optional auxiliary dependent variables integrated along the trajectories (residence time, dose, path length). Used for custom dynamics, tracing streamlines with memory, Poincare maps, kinematics of mechanisms, and teaching problems.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > Mathematical Particle Tracing (pt); API: physics().create("pt", "MathParticle", "geom1")

parameters.name: Formulation
parameters.description: Newtonian | Newtonian, first order | Lagrangian | Hamiltonian | Massless.

parameters.name: Force / Velocity node
parameters.description: Force expression (Newtonian) or velocity field (Massless, e.g. spf.u).

parameters.name: Auxiliary Dependent Variable
parameters.description: Extra ODE per particle: d(rp)/dt = expr, e.g. residence time or accumulated dose.

parameters.name: Release features / Wall
parameters.description: Same set as the other particle interfaces.

tools.notes: Requires the Particle Tracing Module. Results use the Particle dataset, Particle Trajectories plot (with Color Expression on particle variables), Poincare Map and Phase Portrait plots, and Particle Evaluation derived values.

tools.name: Inlet (particles) / Release (domain) / Release from Boundary
tools.description: Particle release features shared by the tracing interfaces: Inlet releases N particles from a boundary with a spatial distribution (uniform, proportional to a field, mesh based, random, density/expression based) and velocity (expression, normal with speed, Maxwellian, cone, hemispherical, from a field); Release launches particles from domains (grid-like or random positions inside the selection); Release from Boundary (6.x naming varies) and Release from Data File (positions/velocities read from a text file) cover imported initial conditions. All support release times, initial values of auxiliary variables and particle weights for Monte Carlo statistics.
tools.usage: Physics > Charged Particle Tracing / Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow > Inlet (inl1) / Release (rel1) / Release from Data File (reldf1); API: physics("cpt").create("inl1", "Inlet", 2); create("rel1", "Release", 3)

parameters.name: N / Release distribution
parameters.description: Number of particles and how positions are chosen (Uniform, Mesh based, Random, Density).

parameters.name: Initial velocity
parameters.description: Expression | Maxwellian (temperature) | Normal velocity | Conical | From velocity field.

parameters.name: Release times
parameters.description: Single time or list (continuous injection).

parameters.name: Particle weight / Nrel
parameters.description: Number of physical particles per model particle for space-charge and flux statistics.

tools.notes: Requires the Particle Tracing Module. Release from Grid (catalogued with the ray features) uses explicit coordinate lists.

tools.name: Wall (particles) / Outlet (particles)
tools.description: Boundary conditions of the particle tracing interfaces: Wall (default on all exterior boundaries with Freeze) decides between Freeze, Stick, Bounce (specular), Disappear, Diffuse scattering, Mixed diffuse and specular, General reflection (user velocity expression) or Pass through, optionally with a probability, secondary particle emission and, for Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow, wall accumulation/erosion/deposition subnodes and rough walls; Outlet is a Wall preset with Freeze/Disappear and transmission-probability bookkeeping used for counting particles that leave (transmission probability, throughput).
tools.usage: Physics > Charged Particle Tracing > Wall (wall1) / Outlet (out1); API: physics("cpt").create("wall2", "Wall", 2); set("WallCondition", "freeze"|"stick"|"bounce"|"disappear"|"diffuse"|"mixed"|"general"|"passthrough")

parameters.name: WallCondition
parameters.description: freeze | stick | bounce | disappear | diffuse | mixed | general | passthrough.

parameters.name: Primary particle condition / probability
parameters.description: Stochastic mixtures and secondary emission (Secondary Emission subnode with yield and velocity distribution).

parameters.name: Accumulator subnode
parameters.description: Accumulate a particle quantity on the boundary (deposition rate, dose, charge density).

tools.notes: Requires the Particle Tracing Module. Particle status (particlestatus variable) records whether a particle is active, frozen, stuck or disappeared.

tools.name: Drag Force / Electric Force / Magnetic Force (particle forces)
tools.description: Domain force nodes of the particle interfaces: Drag Force (Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow) with Stokes, Schiller-Naumann, Haider-Levenspiel, Oseen, standard drag correlation, Khan-Richardson or user drag laws, Cunningham slip correction and turbulent dispersion (random walk) from a k-epsilon solution; Gravity Force, Brownian Force, Lift Force (Saffman), Thermophoretic, Dielectrophoretic and Acoustophoretic forces; and for charged particles Electric Force and Magnetic Force with fields from es/ec/mf/emw solutions (time-harmonic fields with phase). Forces sum when several nodes overlap.
tools.usage: Physics > Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow > Drag Force (df1) / Gravity Force / Brownian Force / Dielectrophoretic Force; Charged Particle Tracing > Electric Force (ef1) / Magnetic Force (mf1); API: physics("fpt").create("df1", "DragForce", 3); physics("cpt").create("ef1", "ElectricForce", 3)

parameters.name: Drag law
parameters.description: Stokes | SchillerNaumann | HaiderLevenspiel | Oseen | StandardDragCorrelation | KhanRichardson | UserDefined.

parameters.name: u_src / E_src / B_src
parameters.description: Source interface variables for the fluid velocity or fields.

parameters.name: Turbulent dispersion
parameters.description: Continuous random walk / discrete random walk with k, epsilon from the flow solution.

parameters.name: Multiply force by phase angle / use piecewise polynomial recovery
parameters.description: Options for AC fields and accuracy.

tools.notes: Requires the Particle Tracing Module. Fluid-Particle Interaction (multiphysics) feeds the reaction force back to the flow for two-way coupling.

tools.name: Optimization (opt) interface
tools.description: Optimization Module interface that declares the ingredients of a PDE-constrained optimisation problem inside a component: objectives (Global Objective, Integral Objective, Probe Objective, Point Sum Objective), control variables (Global Control Variables, Control Variable Field on domains/boundaries with bounds and discretisation), constraints (Global Inequality Constraint, Integral Inequality Constraint, Pointwise Inequality Constraint) and, for topology and shape optimisation, the Density Model and shape features. The Optimization study step then chooses the solver (gradient-based SNOPT/MMA/IPOPT/Levenberg-Marquardt with adjoint sensitivities, or derivative-free Nelder-Mead, BOBYQA, Coordinate Search).
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > Optimization and Sensitivity > Optimization (opt); Study > Optimization; API: physics().create("opt", "GeneralOptimization", "geom1"); opt.create("gobj1", "GlobalObjective", -1); opt.create("gcv1", "GlobalControlVariables", -1)

parameters.name: Objective nodes
parameters.description: objective expression (global scalar or integrand), maximise/minimise handled at the study level.

parameters.name: Control variable nodes
parameters.description: Names, initial values, scales, lower/upper bounds; field variables with shape function order.

parameters.name: Constraint nodes
parameters.description: Inequality bounds on global or integrated expressions.

parameters.name: Study: Optimization step
parameters.description: Method (SNOPT, MMA, IPOPT, Levenberg-Marquardt, Nelder-Mead, BOBYQA, Coordinate search), tolerance, max iterations, objective and control variable tables (may also reference global Parameters).

tools.notes: Requires the Optimization Module. Gradient-based methods need differentiable objectives (avoid maxop/if); parameter-level optimisation of geometry dimensions must use derivative-free methods because the mesh changes. The 'Optimization' study entry in the earlier chunk covers the study node itself. COMSOL 6.4 removed SNOPT: the study step setting is optmethod = neldermead | bobyqa | cobyla | ego | ipopt | gcmma | mma | lm (older optsolver/snopt calls are migrated to ipopt).

tools.name: Sensitivity (sens) interface
tools.description: Mathematics interface that defines an objective functional and sensitivity (design) variables so that a Sensitivity study step computes the derivatives of the objective with respect to the variables by the forward or adjoint method - without running an optimisation. Used for parameter ranking, gradient checks, tolerance analysis and for sensitivity-based shape/topology studies; results are the variables fsens(var) or the sens() operator evaluations.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > Optimization and Sensitivity > Sensitivity (sens); Study > Sensitivity; API: physics().create("sens", "Sensitivity", "geom1"); sens.create("gobj1", "GlobalObjective", -1); sens.create("gcv1", "GlobalControlVariables", -1)

parameters.name: Objective (Global / Integral / Probe)
parameters.description: Scalar functional whose sensitivity is wanted.

parameters.name: Global Control Variables / Control Variable Field
parameters.description: Variables the derivative is taken with respect to.

parameters.name: Sensitivity study step
parameters.description: Method: Forward (few variables) or Adjoint (many variables, one objective).

tools.notes: Core product includes the Sensitivity interface and study; the Optimization Module is needed for optimisation solvers. Sensitivities with respect to geometry need the Deformed Geometry/shape features of the Optimization Module.

tools.name: Density Model (topology optimization)
tools.description: Domain feature under Component > Definitions > Topology Optimization (6.x; earlier a node of the Optimization interface) that defines a density-based topology optimisation: a control variable field theta_c with Helmholtz filtering (minimum feature size), projection (tanh with slope beta and threshold) and interpolation (SIMP, RAMP, Darcy penalisation) giving the penalised material variable dtopo1.theta_p used in the physics (e.g. E = E0*theta_p^p, or a Brinkman sink for fluids). Combined with the Topology Optimization study step (which uses MMA and beta continuation) and the Filter dataset for smooth plotting and the Export of the result to an STL/mesh geometry.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Topology Optimization > Density Model (dtopo1); Study > Topology Optimization; API: model.component("comp1").common().create("dtopo1", "DensityTopology") (6.x) / physics("opt").create("dm1", "DensityTopology", 3) (older)

parameters.name: Filter radius rmin
parameters.description: Minimum length scale via the Helmholtz filter.

parameters.name: Projection slope beta / threshold
parameters.description: Sharpness of the 0/1 projection, usually ramped with continuation.

parameters.name: Interpolation type / SIMP exponent p
parameters.description: SIMP | RAMP | Darcy with penalisation parameter.

parameters.name: Initial value / volume fraction
parameters.description: Starting density; the volume constraint is an Integral Inequality Constraint on theta_p.

tools.notes: Requires the Optimization Module. Use a structured (mapped/swept) or fine uniform mesh; the Filter dataset (Results) gives a clean 0/1 boundary for verification and the Deformed Geometry / mesh export turns it into a CAD-usable shape.

tools.name: Free Shape Domain / Polynomial Boundary / Free Shape Boundary (shape optimization)
tools.description: Shape optimisation features (Component > Definitions > Shape Optimization in 6.x, Optimization Module) that parametrise a geometry deformation without changing the CAD: Free Shape Domain applies a Deformed Geometry smoothing to selected domains, and on its boundaries Free Shape Boundary (filtered nodal control), Polynomial Boundary (Bernstein polynomial displacement of given order), Transformation (rigid translation/rotation/scaling as control variables), Symmetry and Fixed boundary conditions. The Shape Optimization study step then optimises the boundary displacement with gradient-based solvers, with a maximum displacement and filter radius keeping the mesh valid.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Shape Optimization > Free Shape Domain (fsd1) / Free Shape Boundary (fsb1) / Polynomial Boundary (pb1); Study > Shape Optimization; API: model.component("comp1").common().create("fsd1", "FreeShapeDomain"); common().create("pb1", "PolynomialBoundary")

parameters.name: Maximum displacement dmax
parameters.description: Bound on the boundary movement (scaled control variables).

parameters.name: Filter radius (Free Shape Boundary)
parameters.description: Smoothness of the nodal shape variables.

parameters.name: Polynomial order (Polynomial Boundary)
parameters.description: Number of Bernstein coefficients per direction.

parameters.name: Symmetry/Roller boundaries
parameters.description: Keep the shape on symmetry planes.

tools.notes: Requires the Optimization Module. Objectives and constraints are still defined through the Optimization interface or directly in the study step's tables; export the optimised shape with Results > Export > Mesh or Deformed Geometry > Remesh Deformed Configuration.

tools.name: Weak Form PDE (w)
tools.description: Mathematics interface where the equation is entered directly in weak (variational) form as an integrand containing test functions, e.g. -ux*test(ux) - uy*test(uy) + f*test(u), on domains, boundaries, edges or points (Weak Form Boundary PDE, Edge PDE, Point PDE variants exist). It is the most general way to implement custom physics - nonstandard PDEs, integral constraints, Lagrange multipliers, stabilised formulations - and exactly what the built-in interfaces compile to (visible in Equation View).
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > PDE Interfaces > Weak Form PDE (w); API: physics().create("w", "WeakFormPDE", "geom1"); w.feature("wfeq1").set("weak", "...")

parameters.name: Dependent variables / units
parameters.description: Names, number and units of the fields, source term unit.

parameters.name: Weak Form PDE node > weak
parameters.description: Weak expression using test(), spatial derivative suffixes (ux, uy) and time derivatives (ut).

parameters.name: Discretization
parameters.description: Shape function type and order per variable (Lagrange, discontinuous Lagrange, curl, divergence, Argyris...).

parameters.name: Boundary nodes
parameters.description: Zero Flux (natural), Dirichlet Boundary Condition, Constraint, Flux/Source, Weak Contribution, Periodic Condition.

tools.notes: Core product feature. Sign convention: COMSOL solves weak = 0 with the integrand as given, so the diffusion term appears with a minus sign. Coefficient Form and General Form PDE (already catalogued) are the friendlier templates.

tools.name: Wave Form PDE (wahw)
tools.description: Mathematics interface for first-order hyperbolic conservation laws du/dt + div(Gamma(u)) = f solved with the discontinuous Galerkin (dG) method and explicit Runge-Kutta time stepping (the machinery behind the Time Explicit acoustics, elastic wave and shallow-water interfaces). Use it for custom wave equations, advection problems and Euler-type systems where matrix-free explicit stepping scales to very large meshes; Flux/Source and Lax-Friedrichs numerical flux settings define the boundary behaviour.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > PDE Interfaces > Wave Form PDE (wahw); Study > Time Dependent; API: physics().create("wahw", "WaveFormPDE", "geom1")

parameters.name: Wave Form PDE node
parameters.description: Conservative flux Gamma, source f, damping/mass coefficient da; Lax-Friedrichs flux parameter.

parameters.name: Discretization
parameters.description: Discontinuous Lagrange elements (order up to 4).

parameters.name: Flux / Source boundary, Absorbing Layers
parameters.description: Boundary conditions and outgoing-wave damping.

tools.notes: Core product feature. Time step is CFL limited and chosen automatically by the Time Explicit solver; the mesh should be as uniform as possible because the smallest element dictates the step.

tools.name: Boundary ODEs and DAEs (bode) / Domain ODEs and DAEs (dode)
tools.description: Mathematics interfaces adding ordinary differential or algebraic equations that are distributed over a selection (one ODE per mesh node/point of the domain, boundary, edge or point), with no spatial derivatives: surface coverage of adsorbates on an electrode, local damage or ageing variables, wall-film thickness, rate equations of a chemistry that varies in space, or pointwise auxiliary equations coupling to another interface. They complement Global ODEs and DAEs (single scalar equations, already catalogued) and are cheaper than a full PDE.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > ODE and DAE Interfaces > Boundary ODEs and DAEs (bode) / Domain ODEs and DAEs (dode); API: physics().create("bode", "BoundaryODE", "geom1"); physics().create("dode", "DomainODE", "geom1")

parameters.name: Distributed ODE node
parameters.description: Source f, damping/mass coefficients (da, ea) in the form ea*utt + da*ut = f.

parameters.name: Dependent variable / units
parameters.description: Name and unit of the local variable.

parameters.name: Discretization
parameters.description: Lagrange or discontinuous shape functions; order 1 often suffices.

parameters.name: Algebraic Equation node
parameters.description: For pure DAE constraints f = 0.

tools.notes: Core product features. Use Events (ev) for discontinuous switching in ODEs and the Time Dependent solver's algebraic-variable settings for DAEs.

tools.name: Events (ev)
tools.description: Mathematics interface for discontinuities in time-dependent simulations: Explicit Events fire at given times (periodic or listed) and Implicit Events fire when a condition expression changes sign, and both can reinitialise discrete states (Discrete States node) or dependent variables and change parameters; the solver detects the event, stops exactly at it and restarts consistently. Used for switching circuits and controllers (thermostats, PWM), impact and contact switching, batch reactor dosing and any if-then logic that must not be smeared over a time step.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > ODE and DAE Interfaces > Events (ev); API: physics().create("ev", "Events", "geom1"); ev.create("ds1", "DiscreteStates", -1); ev.create("impl1", "ImplicitEvent", -1)

parameters.name: Discrete States
parameters.description: Named state variables with initial values, changed by events (e.g. heater_on).

parameters.name: Indicator States
parameters.description: Continuous indicator expressions used by implicit events (e.g. T - T_set).

parameters.name: Implicit Event: condition / reinitialization
parameters.description: Logical condition on indicators and the assignment executed when it becomes true.

parameters.name: Explicit Event: start / period
parameters.description: Fixed times with optional period and the reinitialisation.

tools.notes: Core product feature. Discrete states are piecewise constant in time; using them in expressions avoids the Newton problems of if() switches. The Time-Dependent solver must not use strict steps that skip the event detection (default settings handle it).

tools.name: Curvilinear Coordinates (cc)
tools.description: Mathematics interface that computes a smooth, geometry-following vector field (and the associated local coordinate system) inside complex domains by the Diffusion, Elasticity, Flow or User-defined method with Inlet/Outlet/Wall boundary features, e.g. to define fibre directions in a curved composite blade, winding directions in a non-trivially shaped coil (Coil Geometry Analysis uses the same idea), or anisotropic conductivity in muscle tissue. The resulting Curvilinear System is then selected in material or physics nodes.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > Curvilinear Coordinates (cc); Definitions > Coordinate Systems > Curvilinear System (auto); API: physics().create("cc", "CurvilinearCoordinates", "geom1"); cc.create("diff1", "Diffusion", 3)

parameters.name: Method node
parameters.description: Diffusion | Elasticity | Flow | User Defined, with Inlet and Outlet boundaries defining the field direction.

parameters.name: Create base vector system
parameters.description: Option producing the Curvilinear System coordinate system (cc.e1x...).

parameters.name: Normalize vector field
parameters.description: Unit vectors for use as directions.

tools.notes: Core product feature. Solve it in its own Stationary study step before the physics that uses the coordinate system.

tools.name: Wall Distance (wd)
tools.description: Mathematics interface solving a modified Eikonal equation for the reciprocal wall distance G, giving the distance to the nearest wall (wd.wallDistance) everywhere in the domain; it is what the turbulence models (k-omega, SST, SA, low-Re) use through the Wall Distance Initialization study step, and it can be used stand-alone for distance-dependent properties (e.g. near-wall damping, coating thickness, mesh size expressions).
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > Classical PDEs > Wall Distance (wd); Study > Wall Distance Initialization; API: physics().create("wd", "WallDistance", "geom1"); wd.create("wall1", "Wall", 2)

parameters.name: Wall node
parameters.description: Boundaries counted as walls.

parameters.name: Reference length / smoothing parameter
parameters.description: Controls the smoothness of the distance field.

tools.notes: Core product feature (added automatically by turbulent-flow interfaces that need it).

tools.name: Deformed Geometry (dg) vs Moving Mesh (ale)
tools.description: The two frame-deformation mechanisms: Deformed Geometry moves the material frame relative to the geometry frame to represent physical shape change of the domain itself - material removal/addition (etching, deposition, corrosion, ablation), shape optimisation, parametrised geometry morphing - and is set up under Component > Definitions > Deformed Geometry (Free Deformation, Prescribed Deformation, Prescribed Normal Mesh Velocity, Deforming Domain with Hyperelastic smoothing); Moving Mesh moves the spatial frame relative to the material frame for ALE problems where the material stays the same but its boundaries move (FSI, free surfaces, moving actuators). Physics interfaces are written in the frame appropriate to them, so choosing the right mechanism keeps conservation and material properties consistent.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Deformed Geometry > Free Deformation / Prescribed Deformation / Prescribed Normal Mesh Velocity; Component > Definitions > Moving Mesh > ...; API: model.component("comp1").common().create("dgfree1", "FreeDeformationDG") (tags/types per submenu) or the legacy interfaces physics().create("dg", "DeformedGeometry", "geom1") / physics().create("ale", "MovingMesh", "geom1")

parameters.name: Smoothing type
parameters.description: Laplace | Winslow | Hyperelastic | Yeoh.

parameters.name: Boundary conditions
parameters.description: Prescribed Mesh Displacement/Velocity, Prescribed Normal Mesh Velocity (e.g. etch rate), Fixed, Free, Symmetry.

parameters.name: Remeshing
parameters.description: Automatic Remeshing (time-dependent) or Remesh Deformed Configuration (creates a new mesh from the deformed state).

tools.notes: Core product feature. Exact API type names of the 6.x Definitions-based nodes vary (check a Java model file saved from the GUI); the Reference Manual chapter Deformed Geometry and Moving Mesh documents both mechanisms. Results on the deformed configuration are shown by default (spatial frame); use the material frame in the dataset settings for undeformed plots.

tools.name: Weak Contribution / Weak Constraint / Pointwise Constraint / Global Constraint
tools.description: Generic equation-building nodes available in every physics interface (under More > or via Show More Options > Equation-Based Contributions): Weak Contribution adds an arbitrary weak-form integrand to the interface's equations on domains/boundaries/edges/points (extra source terms, custom boundary conditions, Lagrange-multiplier couplings, energy terms); Weak Constraint and Pointwise Constraint impose R = 0 constraints either with Lagrange multipliers (accurate reaction forces) or pointwise elimination; Global Constraint adds one scalar equation such as an integral condition (total current = I0) that determines an auxiliary global variable. They let you extend built-in physics without the Physics Builder.
tools.usage: Physics > (More) > Weak Contribution (weak1) / Weak Constraint / Pointwise Constraint / Global Constraint (enable 'Equation-Based Contributions' in Show More Options); API: physics("ht").create("weak1", "WeakContribution", 3); create("gcon1", "GlobalConstraint", -1); create("pc1", "PointwiseConstraint", 2)

parameters.name: weakExpression
parameters.description: Integrand with test() functions, e.g. -Q_extra*test(T).

parameters.name: Auxiliary Dependent Variable subnode
parameters.description: Adds a new field/Lagrange multiplier used in the contribution.

parameters.name: constraintExpression (Pointwise/Weak Constraint)
parameters.description: Expression R that is forced to zero; constraint type unidirectional/bidirectional.

parameters.name: Global Constraint expression
parameters.description: Scalar equation, e.g. intop1(ec.nJ) - I0.

tools.notes: Core product features. Global Constraint needs a global variable to solve for - typically a Global ODEs and DAEs variable or a terminal voltage set to that variable. Constraints on boundaries shared by other constraints can conflict; check the Equation View.

tools.name: Equation View
tools.description: Hidden subnode of every physics node (Show More Options > Equation View) that lists the variables, shape functions, weak expressions and constraints that the node generates, with editable fields so individual variable definitions or weak terms can be overridden without changing the whole feature. It is the way to inspect what COMSOL actually solves, to replace a built-in property expression (e.g. add a custom conductivity variable) and to learn the naming of internal variables for postprocessing.
tools.usage: Model Builder > Show More Options > Equation View, then expand the physics feature > Equation View; API: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").feature("solid1").featureInfo("info").set("varname", "expr") and .setWeak(...)

parameters.name: Variables table
parameters.description: Name, expression, unit, description; editable (yellow) after change, Reset Equation restores.

parameters.name: Shape Functions
parameters.description: Field names, frame, order.

parameters.name: Weak Expressions / Constraints
parameters.description: Integrands and constraint expressions per entity level.

tools.notes: Overrides are fragile across versions and are lost when the feature's settings change substantially; prefer Weak Contribution or Variables nodes for permanent customisation. The Physics Builder is the tool for packaging such changes into reusable interfaces.
